chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr al-Hajari, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'What is the right of the Muslim upon the Muslim?' He said to me, 'There are seven obligatory rights. From them, there is no right except that it is obligatory upon him. If he wastes any of them, he exits from the Wilayah of Allah and His obedience, and there is no share for Allah in him.'

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what are they?' He said, 'O Mu'alla! I am affectionate towards you. I fear that you will waste (them) and not preserve, and you will learn but not act.' I said to him, 'There is no strength except with Allah.'

He said: 'The easiest of them is that you love for him what you love for yourself, and dislike for him what you dislike for yourself. And the second right is that you avoid his anger, follow his pleasure, and obey his command. And the third right is that you support him with your self, your wealth, your tongue, your hand, and your leg.'

And the fourth right is that you become his eye, his guide, and his mirror. And the fifth right is that you are not satiated while he is hungry, nor you quenched while he is thirsty, nor you clothed while he is naked. And the sixth right is that if you have a servant and your brother does not have a servant, it is obligatory that you send your servant so he washes his clothes, prepares his food, and spreads his bed.

And the seventh right is that you fulfill his oath, answer his call, visit his sick, and attend his funeral. And when you know that he has a need, you hasten to fulfill it, and do not force him to ask you for it, but you hasten with a hastening. So when you do that, your Wilayah is linked with his Wilayah, and his Wilayah with your Wilayah.

key_terms.تُبَادِر: To hasten or rush to do something

ai.seo_question: What are the seven obligatory rights of a Muslim upon another Muslim according to Imam al-Sadiq (as)?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details seven comprehensive rights, emphasizing that their neglect causes one to exit the Wilayah of Allah. The rights progress from internal spiritual alignment—loving for others what one loves for oneself—to tangible social obligations, including material assistance, serving as a guide and mirror, and fulfilling vows and needs proactively. This framework underscores the Shia concept of Wilayah as an active, mutual bond of loyalty and service rather than merely a static theological status.
